title: "Conventions and interpretation"
format: html
---

## Time and change coordinates

Keep four time choices distinct: the historical climate extraction window, the historical model simulation window, the CMIP6 reference and future windows, and the stress-test simulation window.
The model period must lie within the extracted historical record.
For a like-period plausibility comparison, choose a projection horizon that corresponds to the stress-test window.
The configured first month of the water year affects annual summaries.

In the stress-test grid, temperature means are additive changes in °C and precipitation means are multipliers: 0.7 means 30% less precipitation, 1.3 means 30% more.
Monthly settings may differ, and constant and transient trajectories differ in the time at which the full change is reached.
WF2 instead reports temperature change as an absolute difference and precipitation change as a relative difference between its own reference and future windows.
Convert to common axes and periods before placing projection points on a response surface.

## Reading a climate response surface

For a selected location and indicator, each tested climate condition has model responses across the configured realizations.
A response surface displays how that indicator varies across temperature and precipitation changes.
The threshold separating acceptable and vulnerable outcomes is a decision criterion supplied by the assessment, not a property inferred by the model.
The CMIP6 overlay helps assess whether climate-model changes fall near vulnerable conditions; it does not attach probabilities to grid cells or establish that unrepresented conditions are impossible.

Separate uncertainty from the stochastic weather realizations, differences across climate projections, and uncertainty in the hydrological model, forcing, observations, and thresholds.
More realizations improve sampling of weather variability but do not remove structural or input-data error.
Use the historical evaluation, where observations exist, when judging how much confidence to place in absolute discharge values.

## Traceability and limits

The scenario collection identifies generated runs and perturbation settings; a simulation experiment records the selected collection and model; a metric set records definitions and source responses.
Join indicator `run_group_id` through `metric_run_lookup.csv` to the collection's `scenario_run_lookup.csv`, then join `st_id` to `perturbation_lookup.csv`.
Keep the identifiers as text, including leading zeros.
The case with an empty `st_id` is the unperturbed reference.
See [Reading the outputs](../guide/outputs.qmd) for the exact layout.

Return levels are GEV fits to groups of simulated years and should be used as screening indicators.
The supplied benchmark covers limited synthetic conditions, offers no basin-specific guarantee, and does not provide uncertainty intervals.
Read `return_level_validation` in `metrics.json` and the corresponding `return_level_benchmark.json` before interpretation.
Short example runs are useful for execution checks, not return-period inference or engineering design.
